p1_findings.title: Three claimed dynamic counter oracles are direct copies of DUT debug events, not independent predictions
evidence: tb_m528_dw1rw/tb_m528_dead_write_only_1rw_product_capture_r2.sv:448-460 increments oracle_macro_reads, oracle_forwards and oracle_deadline_holds directly from debug_scratch_read_event, debug_forward_event and debug_deadline_hold_event.
The same values are only compared back to count_macro_reads, count_forwards and count_deadline_holds at lines 556-559; a common-mode event-generation error and counter error therefore passes.
oracle_issue_stalls at lines 413-414 is derived from DUT issue_data_ready rather than an independently reconstructed sink/parent/deadline/queue readiness model.

The independent reference_parent_edges total and conservation check constrain reads+forwards only; they do not independently validate the read-versus-forward split or deadline-hold count required by the request.
p1_findings.impact: The repaired package correctly proves matcher parents/live writes/dead elisions from stimulus, but it still cannot substantiate its claim of an independent deterministic microevent/counter oracle. A wrong arbitration classification can be mirrored by the debug pulse and architectural counter and remain invisible.
p1_findings.minimum_repair: Build a cleanroom cycle model of stable row order, written rows, earliest unprefetched edge, two slots plus pending reservation, no-consume-credit, one-cycle macro response and sink readiness. Predict macro read, forward, deadline hold and stall from that model without reading DUT debug/queue/live/internal signals, then compare predicted pulses/totals to DUT outputs and counters. The independent model must be reset and closed per epoch.

p1_findings.title: The mandatory stalled-RAW-recovery minimum can be satisfied by an unrelated later forward
evidence: tb_m528_dw1rw/tb_m528_dead_write_only_1rw_product_capture_r2.sv:481-484 sets saw_stalled_raw_q permanently after any stalled_raw event and increments cov_stalled_raw_recovery on every later forward.
saw_stalled_raw_q is not cleared on recovery, task completion, epoch change, or after a bounded window; it persists across the complete normal multi-task suite.

The SVA diagnostic cover at verif_m528_dw1rw/m528_dead_write_only_1rw_product_capture_assertions_r2.sv:225 requires a forward within 1..8 cycles, but the runner parses only the TB summary and does not consume SVA coverage.
p1_findings.impact: The exact coverage token can report stalled_raw_recovery>=1 even when the stalled same-address dependency never recovers, violating one of the eleven launch-blocking minima.
p1_findings.minimum_repair: Track the stalled consumer/parent/epoch and a bounded age, require the matching recovery event within the frozen window, clear the pending recovery state on the match or timeout, and fatal on timeout. Only that causally matched recovery may increment the parsed coverage field.

p1_findings.title: The future VCS runner does not enforce an all-other-run-counts-zero launch admission
evidence: dc_handoff/scripts/run_vcs_m530_m528_dead_write_only_1rw_r2_exact_sha.sh:121-134 promises exactly one VCS run and no synthesis/formal/power/CPU/GPU work.
The rejection loop checks only dc_runs, formality_runs, ptpx_runs, cpu_production_runs and gpu_runs.

pt_runs is omitted even though PT is explicitly forbidden by the source request; iverilog_runs, verilator_runs, cpu_runs and network_or_remote_jobs are also not rejected, and the JSON admission is not checked against a closed authorization-key set.
p1_findings.impact: A double-sealed launch object can satisfy this runner while carrying nonzero authorization for PT or another forbidden side attempt, defeating the required one-attempt identity separation.
p1_findings.minimum_repair: Freeze the launch-admission schema and require vcs_runs==1 while every other run/job counter is explicitly present and zero, including iverilog, Verilator, DC, Formality, PT, PTPX, CPU, GPU and remote/network. Reject unknown authorization keys or bind a strict independently reviewed schema.

p2_findings.finding: The malformed parent-only directed test does not first prove an otherwise-accepting state: sink readiness and matching-parent authority are not forced/checked before attack_parent_only_nonzero_mode is enabled.
p2_findings.impact: Static RTL inspection closes the P0 in this review, but the eventual regression could pass because parent or sink backpressure, rather than preaccept_protocol_ok, blocked the beat.
p2_findings.future_action: Before the attack, force or wait for matching_parent_authoritative, psum_write_ready, row_complete_ready and legal-zero issue_data_ready; then toggle only the malformed payload and prove that readiness and every current-beat architectural event disappear before the sticky fault.

p2_findings.finding: The exact foundry SRAM updates Q after the read clock edge while the queue captures a combinational slot-next value on the following edge; consecutive reads depend on the intended old-Q sampling order around the foundry model's clock event.
p2_findings.impact: This is not a static proof of failure and is appropriately left for the positive foundry-model VCS gate, but no claim of a verified one-cycle macro response is allowed before that run and its independent hammer.
p2_findings.future_action: In the repaired functional VCS attempt, require directed consecutive macro reads with distinct data/addresses and exact response identity/data checking. If event ordering is ambiguous, add an explicit response capture boundary without changing the one-lookahead/1RW architecture and subject it to a new static hammer.

recommendation.reason: A static PASS requires P0=0 and P1=0; this exact r2 source identity has three P1 findings.
recommendation.required_next_gate: A newly admitted source-only repair identity followed by a fresh independent read-only static hammer. Do not overwrite or reseal M529 r1 or M530 r2.
